title: Servo prep (lesson 7). Timer1, fast PWM, 16 MHz clock, prescaler 8. Which ICR1 (TOP) gives a 50 Hz period?
explain: Timer clock = 16 MHz / 8 = 2 MHz. 50 Hz means 20 ms = 40000 ticks. The counter goes 0 … TOP, so it has TOP + 1 steps. TOP = 39999. Forgetting the -1 makes the period 0.5 µs too long.

title: Arduino Uno, int is 16-bit (int16_t here). Scale a 10-bit ADC value to 8-bit PWM. What does this print?
explain: 800 * 255 = 204000 does not fit in 16 bits. It wraps to 7392. Then 7392 / 1023 = 7, not 199. Use long: (long)value * 255 / 1023. Or just shift right by 2.

title: Next topic: interrupts. On an 8-bit AVR, an ISR does ticks++ (uint16_t). loop() reads ticks without any protection. What can go wrong?
options: Nothing. A read is one instruction.
loop() can read the low byte before and the high byte after the ISR. The value is wrong.
The compiler refuses to build it.
explain: A 16-bit read takes two 8-bit loads. If the ISR fires between them, you get half old, half new. Example: 0x00FF becomes 0x01FF, not 0x0100. Fix: disable interrupts for the read, and keep the variable volatile.

title: 5 V supply, red LED drops 2 V. You wanted 15 mA, so you calculated 200 Ω. You only have 220 Ω. What is the LED current?
explain: I = (5 − 2) / 220 = 13.6 mA. The resistor sees only the voltage that is left after the LED: 3 V, not 5 V. A slightly bigger resistor is safe. It only makes the LED a bit dimmer.

title: 7805 regulator, 9 V battery in, 5 V out, the load takes 100 mA. How much power does the 7805 turn into heat?
explain: A linear regulator burns the voltage difference: (9 − 5) V × 0.1 A = 0.4 W. The load gets 0.5 W. So 44% of the battery power is lost. Fine for a lesson, bad for a battery device.

title: Your LDR night light with ONE threshold: LED on if value < 320. The light is near the threshold and noisy. How often does the LED toggle?
explain: Every sample crosses 320, so the LED flips almost every time: 6 toggles in 7 samples. With two thresholds, for example on below 300 and off above 350, it would not toggle at all. This is hysteresis.

title: STM32 EXTI: connect PB5 to EXTI line 5. Each EXTICR register has four 4-bit fields. What does this print (port B = 1)?
explain: Four pins per register: index = pin / 4 = 1 (EXTICR[1]). Field position = (pin % 4) * 4 = 4 bits. Port B = 1, so you write 1 << 4 = 0x10. Clear the old 4 bits first, then OR the new value.

title: Your Reset_Handler. A variable right after .bss sometimes becomes 0. Tap the bug.
explain: _ebss is the address AFTER the last .bss word. With <= the loop also clears one word past .bss. That word may be another variable. The copy loop above uses < correctly.

pr.title: Simplify the timeout check
pr.author: dev-anna
pr.body: elapsed is small, so int is enough. Removed the unsigned long.

explain: On Arduino Uno int is 16-bit (max 32767). When 33 s or more pass, elapsed goes negative and the check fails. millis() is unsigned long. Keep the same type for the subtraction.

title: Before interrupts: 4 rules for shared variables
bullets: volatile: the compiler must re-read the variable every time. Without it, a loop may never see the ISR change.
volatile does NOT make access atomic. A 16-bit read on an 8-bit CPU takes two loads.
Short critical section: disable interrupts, copy the value, enable interrupts, then use the copy.
Keep the ISR short: set a flag or count, do the real work in loop().
